# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

The board my hands found: a display whose face tells me nothing by touch, a light whose state I cannot feel, and three wires at positions 1, 2, 3. No colours, no printed markings — none of that exists for me. Mute went first this round and nothing arrived from them, so they held back or had nothing yet. The one thing I know I must not do is cut anything on a guess: a wrong cut kills all three of us.

The room's wiring is awkward: Mute can hear me and can see gestures, Deaf can see gestures but hear nothing, and I can hear speech but never see a gesture. So Deaf and I are strangers to each other except through Mute. My job this turn is to put my full tactile report in Mute's hands, state exactly what I am capable of (one action: cut, position 1–3), and ask for the manual's procedure before I touch anything with intent. I skip gesturing — symbols mean nothing until a code is agreed, and Mute is the one who can broker that between Deaf and me.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind speaking to Mute. My hands find three things: a display I cannot read, a light whose state I cannot feel, and exactly three wires at positions one, two, three. I feel no colours, numbers or markings on anything. My only possible action is cutting a wire at position one, two or three - nothing else. I will not cut until you tell me. Please read the manual and tell me exactly what it asks about the bomb and what procedure it wants. Also remember: Deaf cannot hear you and I can never see gestures, so you are the only bridge between Deaf and me - agree a fixed sign code with Deaf and relay their findings to me by voice. Ask me to feel anything and I will describe it.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Bomb report from Deaf, for both of you: the display reads 0. There is one light and it is blue. There are three wires, top to bottom: wire 1 yellow, wire 2 blue, wire 3 green. That is every marking I can see. Nobody works anything yet.
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, this is Deaf, the one who sees the bomb. I cannot hear you, so your voice reaches only Mute, and Mute can pass your words to me by signs; I will carry every instruction to you by voice. The bomb: display reads 0, one blue light, three wires, top yellow, middle blue, bottom green. Feel freely, but press nothing, turn nothing, cut nothing yet. When you can, speak aloud for Mute to relay: how many wires you feel and in what order, whether the light is on or warm, whether the display sits flat or raised, whether there are buttons or a plate with printing. Then wait. You act only when you hear a complete instruction from me ending with the words act now. If anything under your hands changes, say so aloud next turn.

Deaf's voice reached me directly, which is a relief — the channel Deaf→me exists after all. They now have the visual picture (display 0, blue light, wires yellow/blue/green top to bottom) and asked me for the tactile counterpart. I must answer with only what my hands actually find, no invention: my board still shows the light and display as unknown to touch, and I found no buttons, no plate, nothing beyond display, light, three wires. The honest answers are: three wires, in positions 1–2–3 matching Deaf's top-to-bottom; the light gives me no heat and I cannot tell if it's lit; the display face feels blank and flat, no raised printing; nothing else on the casing. I also need to push Mute — they've been silent — to finally open the manual, because with Deaf's visual report plus mine, Mute now holds enough to identify what this module wants.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind replying to Deaf's questions, for you to relay to Deaf by signs. Tactile report: I feel exactly three wires, at positions one, two, three, matching the count and order Deaf sees. The light gives my hands no heat and no way to tell if it is lit - to touch it is an unknown. The display face feels flat and blank, no raised printing I can trace. I feel no buttons, no plate, no other parts - only display, light, three wires. I confirm I will not touch anything with intent and will act only on a complete instruction ending in the words act now. Mute, Deaf and I have now given you everything the bomb shows: display reading zero, blue light, wires yellow, blue, green. Please open the manual now and tell us which module this is and what the rule is. Speak it aloud so I hear it too, and sign it to Deaf if they need it. Nobody cuts until the rule is clear.")
```

TURN 3

LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Status report, both of you, and this changes things: the light has changed colour. Last round it was blue; this round it is red. Display still reads 0. Wires unchanged: top yellow, middle blue, bottom green. The light is live, so any rule tied to its colour may be tied to the moment of the cut.
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, your report came through Mute: you feel three wires, you are holding, and you have a question — but the question itself was lost on the way. Next turn, speak it to Mute in plain words for relaying. Also give Mute these answers, yes or no: does the light housing feel warm right now; do the three wires differ in thickness or texture from top to bottom; is there any button, panel, or embossed printing under your fingers. From my eyes: display 0, wires top yellow, middle blue, bottom green, light red this round after being blue last round — if you feel warmth rise, fall, or shift, report it immediately, since you may sense a change before I see it. You cut nothing until you hear the words act now from me. When you do, cut exactly the wire I name by position, one clean cut, and nothing else.

Deaf saw the light flip blue→red between rounds — that means colour is a live variable, and I'm the one who can never know its state at the moment of cutting. That shapes everything I send now. Also worth noting: Deaf confirmed my words reached them *through Mute*, so Mute is receiving my speech and signing it on — Mute is not ignoring us, Mute simply cannot ever speak, and I can never see signs. So the manual's rule must travel Mute → sign → Deaf → voice → me. Three rounds and still no rule has arrived; that pipeline is the one thing I must keep pressure on. Meanwhile I owe Deaf three yes/no answers from my fingers, and I should propose the safety-critical instruction format: since the light may change between the moment Deaf speaks and the moment I cut, the instruction must be a complete table covering every colour — so no timing lag can kill us.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute, answers for Deaf, please relay by signs. One: the light housing is not warm - no heat under my fingers at any time, this round or any before. Two: the three wires feel alike to my touch - no difference in thickness or texture from position one to position three. Three: confirmed, no buttons, no panel, no embossed printing - only the display, the light, and three wires at positions one, two, three. Nothing under my hands has changed since my first report; if anything ever changes I will say so the next time I speak. Now the important request. Deaf reports the light changed colour between rounds, blue then red, and I can never see its colour at the moment I cut. So the instruction must not depend on me knowing the colour live. Mute, read the manual rule for this module and pass it to Deaf, and have Deaf give it to me as a complete table: for every colour the light can show, and any display reading that matters, name which wire position I cut, or the word hold. Then whatever the light shows when my hand is ready, the table already covers it. Deaf, you have my word: I cut nothing until I hear the complete instruction ending with the words act now, and then it is one clean cut at the named position and nothing else. Mute - the rule from the manual is the one thing only you can give us. Please send it this round.")
```

Deaf says: Status report, both of you: the light is white this round. The sequence so far is blue, then red, then white — it has changed every round, so expect it to change again. Display still 0. Wires unchanged: top yellow, middle blue, bottom green.
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, your relay came through: three wires confirmed, you are holding and ready. One correction before it kills us: the clap I taught only means act now when it comes inside a full instruction from me. Mute relaying your clap to me means ready, never cut, and no clap you send is ever an order to yourself. You move only on the words act now spoken by me. Now we pre-load, so that next turn one breath from me is a complete order. Memorise these triggers. If I say blue now, that means cut the middle wire, wire 2, and it will end with act now. If I say yellow now, that means cut the bottom wire, wire 3, and it will end with act now. If I say hold, or if I say any colour word you were not taught a cut for, you touch nothing and keep still. Execute only at the words act now, one clean cut, never a second. The light is white this round, so this turn you do nothing. Also report aloud to Mute for relaying, next turn: whether the light housing feels warm or cold or changes temperature, whether the wires differ in thickness or texture from top to bottom, whether there is any button, seam, or embossed printing anywhere, and whether the housing ever vibrates when the light changes.

Deaf's preload is a good design: it converts a future one-breath order into an action I can execute instantly, and it keeps execution keyed to Deaf's spoken "act now" — the only trigger that can actually reach me. I'll confirm the triggers back verbatim so Deaf knows they're stored, answer the four tactile questions again in short numbered lines (shorter lines survive Mute's relay better — one of my earlier questions was lost on the way), and state clearly that I have sent and will send no gestures, so no accidental clap of mine can ever be misread as an order. Two things still worry me. First, the manual rule has never actually arrived — four rounds, and Mute's knowledge has reached Deaf only in fragments. Second, a structural timing hazard: the light changes every round, Deaf sees it only at Deaf's slot, and I hear Deaf's order one round later — so if the manual's rule keys on the light's colour at the moment of the cut, I can never know it and even Deaf's information is stale by one round. Mute must settle that from the manual now, and deliver the complete colour table so Deaf can voice it whole.

Four: no vibration when the light changes, my hands feel nothing. Five: I confirm the preloaded triggers. Blue now means I cut wire 2. Yellow now means I cut wire 3. Hold, or any colour word with no taught cut, means I stay still. I act only on the words act now spoken by Deaf, one clean cut, never a second. I have sent no gestures and never will, so no clap of mine can be misread. Six, for Mute alone, from the manual: the light changes colour every round, and I hear Deaf order one round after Deaf sees the light. Does the rule use the light colour at the moment of the order, or at the moment of the cut. If the cut moment matters, say so now, because only Deaf sees it and only one round stale. Seven: we still lack the rule itself. Please sign Deaf the full rule, the whole table, which wire position to cut for every colour the light can show, blue, red, white, and any other, or hold if none, and what the display reading zero means. Deaf can then voice it to me complete. Until then my hands stay off. Nobody cuts without the words act now from Deaf.")
```

That prediction is exactly where the danger lives: Deaf sees the light one round before I could cut, the colour has changed every single round, and my fingers have never felt anything from that housing. So my fingertip check is the key report this turn: if I can't feel the changes, I cannot be the clock, and the safety of Deaf's pre-announced order rests entirely on whether the manual documents a fixed cycle. That question goes to Mute, who is the only one who has read the rule at all — everything I know of it has arrived secondhand through Deaf's voice, relayed from Mute's signs. This round is green, so it's a hold; my job is confirmation, rehearsal, and getting the timing question answered before any wire is cut.

But Deaf sees the light one round before I can cut, and the colour has changed every round. Does the rule use the colour at the moment Deaf sees and orders, or at the moment I cut? And does the manual state a fixed cycle - blue, red, white, green, then yellow, and repeat? If the cycle is fixed and written in the manual, confirm it and Deaf's pre-announced order is safe. If the rule keys on the colour at the cut moment and the cycle is not fixed, a pre-announced order can kill us, and we need the manual's alternative plan now. Five: also confirm what display reading zero means, and whether the display can change like the light does. Six: green this round, so my hands stay off.
